summary: This program defines a single growPlant function that takes sunlight and water as parameters, then calls it with specific values from main. The function prints the conditions it was given and uses a ternary operator to decide whether the plant is growing or needs care.

lines.text: This is the function call, and the values true and 3 are the arguments. Because the definition asks for a boolean followed by an int, they must be passed in that order and in those types.

lines.text: The two parameters are placeholders for data the function needs from outside, just as a houseplant needs sunlight and water brought to it. Every call supplies fresh values without any change to the code inside.
The soil is provided inside the function itself, so it is not a parameter. Some things a function needs are its own; only what varies gets passed in.

A ternary operator evaluates the condition and produces one of two values: "Growing" when there is sunlight and the water level is at least 3, otherwise "Needs care". It is a compact stand-in for a full if/else that assigns a value.
